The '''MD-CH1 Droid''' was a model of small bipedal [[Droid/Legends|droid]] available during the [[Third Galactic War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]].<ref name="LotS">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Legacy of the Sith]]''</ref> The MD-CH1 Droid was associated with the Sith Empire, and more specifically [[Darth Malgus]].<ref name="SE" />

MD-CH1 Droids were plated in a [[Color/Legends|silver]] and black colors. The droid's head had a [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptor]] that was red in coloration.<ref name="SE" />

{{Droid-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
On [[February 4]], [[2022]], the MD-CH1 Droid was announced to appear<ref name="SE" /> in the [[2022]] expansion [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Legacy of the Sith|''Legacy of the Sith'']] to [[BioWare]]'s [[2011]] [[Star Wars video games|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]], ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''.<ref name="LotS" /> The droid was made available as a minipet in the Darth Malgus-themed "Legacy of the Sith: Digital Collector’s Edition" bundle.<ref name="SE" />

The MD-CH1 Droid was designed by concept artist [[Bradley W. Lewis]], who first revealed on his ArtStation account that the droid was inspired by a set of [[Macrobinoculars/Legends|macrobinoculars]], using similar but slightly different sets of camera parts than the ones used in the original prop from [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|A New Hope]]. He also use other vintage camera gear for inspiration such as a vintage [[Wikipedia:Graflex|Graflex]] side grip and vintage lamp parts for the legs. Lewis stated that droid was nicknamed "murderchicken one," which led to the in-universe designation MD-CH1.<ref name="Concept">{{ArtStation|username=nonentity|url=artwork/DA1vAn|name=[[Bradley W. Lewis|Bradley Lewis]]|text=SWTOR &#124; MD-CH1 Minipet Droid|quote=MD-CH1, or "murderchicken one" This is another asset from our 10th anniversary SWTOR digital collector's edition I made. This was inspired by a set of macrobinoculars, using similar but slightly different sets of camera parts than the ones used in the original prop from A New Hope. I also use other vintage camera gear such as a vintage Graflex side grip and vintage lamp parts for the legs. The camera lens eye has several individually animated segments that rotate randomly, and the feet are inspired by Malgus' lightsaber blades. This minipet droid took me one week from start to completion covering concept, model, material and texture, and animation of eyepiece components. It was a test to see what I could build for the game in one week's time.}}</ref>
